subject: Re: AWS Marketplace activation gating, entitlement mapping & reconciliation plan
messages:
From: Sarah Lawrence <sarah.lawrence@acme.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace activation gating and entitlement questions

Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looked great and our PMs are excited to move ahead. Procurement asked me to get a crisp plan for how activation and entitlement will work if we list the Acme UI in AWS Marketplace (SaaS). Two specific asks from legal/finance before we start the marketplace listing process: 

1) Clear mapping from Marketplace Entitlement IDs to our internal subscription model (we use per-seat + optional call-units). We need to understand how the entitlement payload flows into our billing system to avoid double-billing.

2) Reconciliation cadence and tools if Marketplace metering events are delayed (we have month-end closes and need an invoiceable delta rather than a surprise credit).

I'm attaching the initial SOW and our procurement checklist. Can you share a short mutual action plan and confirm whether Redwood can support an invoice-first approach for the first two billing cycles (Acme is a small startup and needs a short invoicing window before switching to Marketplace direct billing)?

Appreciate a timeline we can share with Procurement.

Best,
Sarah
---
Sarah Lawrence
Head of Partnerships, Acme AI
[Attachment: sow-acme-aws-usage-mapping.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace activation gating and entitlement questions

Hi Sarah — thanks for the SOW and the clear asks. We can definitely support Acme on Marketplace; below is a short mutual action plan and the technical artifacts we'll need. I pulled finance and infra into cc to speed things up.

Mutual action plan (high level)
- Week 0: Contract redlines + DocuSign (we'll accept limited invoice terms for months 1–2 as a one-time exception; details below).
- Week 1: Marketplace listing + entitlement mapping spec (Redwood provides an entitlement mapping template).
- Week 2: Activation webhook integration and canary (we'll wire the activation webhook to Acme staging and validate idempotency).
- Week 3: Pilot metering run and reconciliation test (3-day pilot with controlled traffic, then run a reconciliation job).
- Week 4: Go-live and normal metered billing.

What we need from Acme
- Confirm the canonical subscription keys (per-seat id, customer_account_id, optional call_unit meter name) used by your billing system.
- Procurement-signed redlines on the contract (send DocuSign link).
- A staging Marketplace subscription or test SaaS contract so we can validate entitlement-to-billing mapping.

About the invoice-first request
We can provisionally offer net-30 invoice for months 1–2 while marketplace onboarding completes. That will be managed under a temporary purchase order and invoices from Redwood Finance; after the pilot we will transition billing to AWS Marketplace (metered). We will need procurement to sign an invoice addendum to capture this handoff and liability.

Technical notes (short)
- Entitlement payload: Redwood will emit the marketplace entitlement id in every activation event and include a normalized subscription_id field you configure.
- Metering records: We support immediate metering (+ eventual reconciliation). Late event handling: we deliver a reconciliation batch that produces delta reports and either credits or invoices depending on the reconciliation outcome.
- Idempotency: activation webhooks include an event_id; we expect receivers to ack and idempotently apply events.

I'll drop a proposed DocuSign and a short technical spec by EOD. Can we do a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT to align?

Cheers,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace activation gating and entitlement questions

Adding some technical detail from infra to make the pilot smoother. TL;DR: we recommend a gated activation that maps Marketplace Entitlement -> Redwood subscription -> Acme subscription key.

Key implementation notes
- Entitlement mapping: we'll provide a mapping file that links marketplace_entitlement_id -> redwood_subscription_id -> acme_canonical_id. This mapping is a simple CSV for the pilot and a small API call for production.
- Activation webhook: Redwood will POST activation events to the endpoint you provide. Payload includes: event_id, entitlement_id, normalized_subscription_id, timestamp, usage_bucket (if applicable). We will treat POSTs as retried until acked; receivers must respond with 200 and dedupe by event_id.
- Metering and reconciliation: we emit metering events in near-real time to AWS (as required by marketplace metering). For delayed events (replays or late reports) we produce a reconciliation manifest (day-level granularity) and a suggested delta file for your billing system. We can optionally output a one-line invoiceable delta for finance to pick up.
- Canary + rollback: recommend 5% of traffic for 48 hours to validate idempotency and reconciliation. If reconciliation drift > 2% we roll back and investigate.

Operational hooks
- We created a short runbook to validate idempotency and reconciliation: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/aws-marketplace-activation (internal).
- If procurement needs an invoice grace period, finance will require a signed addendum and purchase order in the first week.

Happy to walk the engineering team through the webhook payloads on the call.

—Jordan
Principal Engineer, Integrations
Redwood Inference
